I've farmed this 9.5 mu in Quzhou for 30 years, wheat in winter and maize in summer. I finished middle school, and I learn from the input dealer and watching my neighbors — that's how I know what works.

For wheat this year, I'm planting Jimai 22, same as last year and same as Old Wang next door. It's an improved variety. I put 30 jin of seed per mu — that's 15 kg. For fertilizer, I use one full bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as base dressing, 50 kg per mu. Then at green-up time I spread 15 kg of urea, and at jointing stage another 10 kg of urea. The dealer told me that's about 19 kg of nitrogen, 8 kg of phosphorus, and 8 kg of potassium per mu. I don't do the math myself but I've used this recipe for years. I irrigate three times from my well: once when the wheat turns green in spring, once at jointing, and once at filling stage. I spray pesticides three times — herbicide at tillering, then insecticide and fungicide when it gets warm. Before planting, I rotary till the field. Last year I got about 500 kg per mu, and I expect about the same this year if the weather holds.

For maize, I plant Zhengdan 958, the hybrid everyone uses. Right after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed into the wheat stubble without tilling — no-tillage saves me time and diesel, and everyone does it now. I use about 5 jin of seed per mu, that's 2.5 kg. At planting I put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, then at big trumpet stage I top-dress with 25 kg of urea. That works out to about 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: at big trumpet stage and at filling stage. Three pesticide sprays for weeds and corn borer. I expect around 600 kg per mu.

Fertilizer and chemicals cost me over 300 yuan per mu now — it's a lot. But my family has seven people, and my sons send money from their factory jobs, so I can manage it. I'd rather put on a bit too much than risk a bad harvest. A bad year means losing thousands of yuan; wasting some fertilizer is nothing compared to that. I watch what my neighbors do, and if they're all putting on similar amounts, I do the same. You don't take risks with 9.5 mu when it's been feeding your family for 30 years.
